c.tagline: Temples, tuk-tuks, and street food that never sleeps.

avoid.reason: Classic scams — the "Grand Palace closed"/gem shop, tuk-tuk and taxi-meter refusals, jet-ski/rental damage.
Pickpocketing and drink-spiking in the nightlife areas.

hood_desc: A long, cosmopolitan strip of malls, rooftop bars, international restaurants, and nightlife stretching along the BTS line, popular with expats, nightlife lovers, and mid-range to upscale travelers.
The city's main business and financial district by day that transforms into a buzzing nightlife zone after dark, home to Patpong and a great base for foodies and professionals.
The legendary backpacker enclave of cheap guesthouses, street food, bars, and travel agencies, drawing budget travelers and party-minded backpackers.
A historic riverside area along the Chao Phraya with grand heritage hotels, upscale dining, and easy access to temples, suiting luxury travelers and those seeking old-world charm.
The central shopping district anchored by megamalls like Siam Paragon and MBK, a magnet for shoppers, teens, and anyone wanting to be at the retail and transit heart of the city.

water.note: Avoid drinking from the tap; stick to bottled or filtered water, though ice at restaurants is usually fine.

transit.pay: There is no single card for everything: the BTS uses the Rabbit card (about 200 baht incl. credit, ~US$6, from BTS ticket offices — bring your passport), while single-trip tickets come from station machines. Both BTS (since Aug 2025) and MRT now accept contactless Visa/Mastercard at the gates, which is the easiest option for visitors.
transit.hours: BTS and MRT run about 5:30am to midnight daily with no night trains — use taxis or Grab after hours.

food.name: Pad thai
food.desc: Thailand's national stir-fried noodle dish with prawns, tamarind, egg and crushed peanuts.

places.name: Thipsamai
places.note: Thailand's oldest pad thai shop, since 1966; wrapped-in-egg version is legendary

places.name: Baan Phadthai
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand spot known for refined pad thai with house-made sauce

places.name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu
places.note: Wok-fire specialist with Michelin recognition, near the Old Town classics

food.name: Crab omelette (khai jeaw poo)
food.desc: A fluffy omelette stuffed with lump crab meat, made world-famous by a goggle-wearing street chef.

places.name: Raan Jay Fai
places.note: Bangkok's first Michelin-starred street stall; still cooking, expect long queues

places.name: Here Hai
places.note: Bib Gourmand favorite for crab omelette and crab fried rice per recent reviews

food.name: Boat noodles (kuay teow reua)
food.desc: Intense little bowls of pork or beef noodles in rich, spiced broth, ordered by the stack.

places.name: Pa Yak Boat Noodle
places.note: Most famous shop in the canal-side boat noodle alley

places.name: Thong Smith
places.note: Popular upscale take on boat noodles with wagyu options

food.name: Khao man gai
food.desc: Thai-style Hainanese chicken rice: poached chicken over garlic rice with a punchy ginger-soy sauce.

places.name: Go-Ang Kaomunkai Pratunam
places.note: The pink-shirt Bib Gourmand institution, one of Bangkok's most famous plates

places.name: Kuang Heng
places.note: Green-shirt rival next door, serving chicken rice since 1932

food.name: Tom yum goong
food.desc: Thailand's hot-sour prawn soup with lemongrass, lime leaf and chili, creamy or clear.

places.name: Pee Aor Tom Yum Goong

places.name: Jeh O Chula

food.name: Mango sticky rice
food.desc: Ripe Nam Dok Mai mango with coconut-cream sticky rice, Thailand's best-loved dessert.

places.name: Kor Panich
places.note: Since 1932 and Michelin Bib listed; the city's benchmark mango sticky rice

places.name: Yenly Yours
places.note: Popular modern mango dessert chain, an easy high-quality option

places.name: Make Me Mango
places.note: Stylish mango cafe near Wat Pho, well reviewed by recent visitors

food.name: Thai iced tea (cha yen)
food.desc: Sweet orange-hued black tea with condensed milk over ice, Thailand's signature street drink.

places.name: Cha Tra Mue
places.note: The heritage Thai tea brand's own stands; the classic cha yen benchmark

places.name: On Lok Yun
places.note: 1930s coffee shop loved for old-school Thai tea and breakfast sets

food.name: Ya dong (Thai herbal spirits)
food.desc: Traditional rice-spirit infusions with herbs, reborn in Bangkok's craft bars; drink responsibly.

places.name: Tep Bar
places.note: Stylish bar credited with reviving ya dong, with live Thai music

places.name: Teens of Thailand
places.note: Acclaimed Thai-flavored gin bar in a heritage shophouse, on Asia's best-bar lists

landmarks: Grand Palace
The dazzling former royal residence, with its gilded spires and intricate ornamentation, is Bangkok's most iconic and photographed complex.
Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn)
A porcelain-encrusted riverside temple spire that glows at sunset, offering one of the most iconic views along the Chao Phraya.
Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha)
Home to a colossal 46-meter gold-plated reclining Buddha and Thailand's traditional massage school, this temple is a must-see cultural landmark.
Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew)
Thailand's most sacred temple, housing the revered jade Emerald Buddha within the Grand Palace grounds, dazzles with intricate gilded detail.
Chatuchak Weekend Market
One of the world's largest markets, with thousands of stalls, is a vibrant, colorful must-visit for shopping and street food.
Yaowarat Road (Chinatown)
Bangkok's neon-lit Chinatown strip bursts with street food stalls, gold shops, and lantern-draped storefronts, especially vivid after dark.
Khao San Road
The legendary backpacker street, alive with street food, market stalls, and neon nightlife, is a rite-of-passage Bangkok experience.
Wat Traimit (Golden Buddha)
Houses the world's largest solid-gold Buddha statue, a 5.5-ton, 700-year-old masterpiece rediscovered by accident in the 1950s.
Chao Phraya River
The lifeblood of Bangkok, lined with temples, palaces, and bustling long-tail boats, offers some of the city's best sunset photography.
Jim Thompson House
The elegant teakwood estate of the American silk entrepreneur who vanished mysteriously in 1967 showcases traditional Thai architecture and art.

train.note: Bangkok is famous for its domestic night trains from Krung Thep Aphiwat terminal — sleepers to Chiang Mai, Nong Khai and the south for the islands. Book up to 90 days ahead; lower berths sell out fast. For Malaysia, change to a KTM train at Padang Besar (ktmb.com.my).

bus.note: International coaches leave from Mochit (Northern) Bus Terminal. Bangkok–Cambodia coaches are suspended while the land border remains closed (as of July 2026) — check status or fly. No direct coach to Malaysia; go via Hat Yai or take the train.

ferry.note: Bangkok is a river city with no international ferries. On the water locally, the Chao Phraya Express Boat is the classic way around; for Gulf islands like Koh Samui, take a train or bus south and connect to a ferry at Chumphon or Surat Thani.

half.name: Ayutthaya
half.blurb: A UNESCO-listed former royal capital famous for its sprawling ancient temple ruins and Buddha statues.

half.name: Damnoen Saduak Floating Market
half.blurb: The country's most iconic floating market, where vendors sell fruit and food from wooden canoes.

half.name: Maeklong Railway Market
half.blurb: A market built on live train tracks where stalls fold away each time a train passes through.

half.name: Pattaya
half.blurb: A busy beach resort city drawing crowds for its seaside, nearby islands and lively nightlife.

full.name: Kanchanaburi
full.blurb: Visitors come for the Bridge over the River Kwai, WWII history and Erawan's tiered waterfalls.

full.name: Khao Yai National Park
full.blurb: Thailand's oldest national park, loved for jungle trails, waterfalls and wild elephant sightings.
